parts.text: This question is about nitrogen and compounds of nitrogen.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Ammonia is manufactured by the reaction between nitrogen and hydrogen in the Haber process. The equation is shown. N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g) 2NH 3 (g)

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) State the typical conditions used in the Haber process. temperature .......................................... ° C pressure ............................................... atm [2]

ms.label: 6(a)(v)
ms.text:
M1 (a substance which) increases the rate of a reaction
M2 remains unchanged at the end of the reaction

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Ammonia is converted into nitric acid.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) The first stage is the conversion of ammonia into nitrogen monoxide, NO. The equation is shown. 4NH 3 (g) + 5O 2 (g) 4NO(g) + 6H 2 O(g) The reaction is carried out at a temperature of 900 ° C and a pressure of 7 atm. The forward reaction is exothermic. Using explanations that do not involve cost: ● explain why a temperature less than 900 ° C is not used ............................................................................................................................................. ● explain why a pressure greater than 7 atm is not used. ............................................................................................................................................. [2]

ms.label: 6(b)(i)
ms.text:
temperature change:
M1 low(er) rate (of reaction)
pressure change:
M2 (position of) equilibrium shifts to the left hand side/ towards reactants

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) In the second stage, nitrogen monoxide reacts with water and oxygen to produce nitric acid. Balance the symbol equation for the reaction. .....NO + .....O 2 + .....H 2 O → .....HNO 3 [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) A student makes aqueous copper( II ) nitrate by adding an excess of solid copper( II ) carbonate to dilute nitric acid.

ms.label: 6(c)(i)
ms.text:
CuCO3 + 2HNO3 → Cu(NO3)2 + CO2 + H2O
M1 Cu(NO3)2
M2 correct equation

ms.label: 6(c)(ii)
ms.text:
M1 undissolved solid
M2 effervescence stops on addition of more copper(II) carbonate

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Name one compound, other than copper( II ) carbonate, that can be added to dilute nitric acid to produce aqueous copper( II ) nitrate. ....................................................................................................................................... [1]
